title_en: Chongqing Taihua Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. v. Chongqing Chenguang Industrial Development (Group) Co., Ltd., Chongqing Chenguang Department Store Co., Ltd., and Chongqing Chenguang Hotel Co., Ltd. — dispute over house relocation
ruling_gist_en: Revocation of the business license of an enterprise legal person is an administrative penalty imposed by the administrative authority for industry and commerce on an illegal enterprise legal person in accordance with national industrial and commercial administrative regulations. After the business license of an enterprise legal person is revoked, it shall undergo liquidation in accordance with law. Only after the liquidation process is completed and the business registration is cancelled does the enterprise legal person cease to exist. Whether the enterprise legal person continues to exist should be determined by whether the administrative authority for industry and commerce has cancelled its legal person status. As long as the enterprise has not been cancelled, even if its business license has been revoked, it still retains legal person status and still has the capacity for rights and the capacity to act in litigation, and has the right to conduct litigation activities in its own name.

full_text_en:
Chongqing Taihua Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. v.

Chongqing Chenguang Industrial Development (Group) Co., Ltd.,

Chongqing Chenguang Department Store Co., Ltd., and

Chongqing Chenguang Hotel Co., Ltd.

— dispute over house relocation

[Ruling Summary]

The revocation of a business license of an enterprise as a legal person is an administrative penalty imposed by the administrative authority for industry and commerce on an enterprise legal person that has violated the national industrial and commercial administrative regulations. After the business license of an enterprise legal person is revoked, it shall undergo liquidation in accordance with the law. Only after the liquidation procedure is completed and the industrial and commercial cancellation registration is effected does the enterprise legal person cease to exist. Whether an enterprise legal person continues to exist shall be determined by whether the administrative authority for industry and commerce has cancelled its legal person status. As long as the enterprise has not been cancelled, even if its business license is revoked, it still has legal person status, still has the capacity for rights and capacity to act in litigation, and has the right to conduct litigation activities in its own name.

Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court

(2005) Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 57

Appellant (plaintiff at first instance): Chongqing Taihua Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at Hongyupo, Shigiao Pu Roundabout, Gaoxin District, Chongqing.

Legal representative: Wu Shenggang, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Dong Jiawei, lawyer of Chongqing Hui Ju Law Firm.

Respondent (defendant at first instance): Chongqing Chenguang Industrial Development (Group) Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 33-37 Xiaoxin Street, Shapingba District, Chongqing.

Legal representative: Li Zhigang, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Bai Qiang, lawyer of Chongqing Ju Jie Law Firm.

Respondent (defendant at first instance): Chongqing Chenguang Department Store Co., Ltd., domiciled at Hongyupo, Shigiao Pu, Gaoxin District, Chongqing.

Legal representative: Jia Zhilin, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Bai Qiang, lawyer of Chongqing Ju Jie Law Firm.

Respondent (defendant at first instance): Chongqing Chenguang Hotel Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 1 Yuzhou Road, Shigiao Pu, Gaoxin District, Chongqing.

Legal representative: Jia Zhilin, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Bai Qiang, lawyer of Chongqing Ju Jie Law Firm.

In the case of dispute over house relocation between the appellant, Chongqing Taihua Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Taihua Company), and the respondents, Chongqing Chenguang Industrial Development (Group) Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Chenguang Group), Chongqing Chenguang Department Store Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Chenguang Department Store), and Chongqing Chenguang Hotel Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Chenguang Hotel), the Chongqing High People's Court rendered a civil ruling (2003) Yu Gao Fa Min Chu Zi No. 12 on March 24, 2005. The appellant Taihua Company, dissatisfied with the ruling, appealed to this Court. This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel and opened a hearing in this case on August 4, 2005. Dong Jiawei, agent ad litem for the appellant Taihua Company, and Bai Qiang, agent ad litem for the respondents Chenguang Group, Chenguang Department Store, and Chenguang Hotel, appeared in court for the proceedings. This case is now concluded.

The court of first instance found the following facts after trial:

On September 20, 1992, Chongqing Shangqiao Industrial General Company (hereinafter referred to as Shangqiao Company), Chongqing Shapingba Materials Company (hereinafter referred to as Materials Company), and Taiwanese businessman Bao Yangbo signed the "Contract for the Joint Venture of Chongqing Taihua Real Estate Development Co., Ltd." (hereinafter referred to as the "Joint Venture Contract"), stipulating that Shangqiao Company would contribute the RMB equivalent of USD 820,000, representing 40% of the shares; Materials Company would contribute the RMB equivalent of USD 205,000, representing 10% of the shares; and Bao Yangbo would contribute USD 1,025,000, representing 50% of the shares, jointly establishing Taihua Company. The joint venture term was 10 years, calculated from the date of issuance of the business license. The board of directors was composed of three members, each appointed by the three shareholders: Shangqiao Company, Materials Company, and Bao Yangbo. The chairman of the board was appointed by Bao Yangbo. The term of office for directors and the chairman was three years, renewable upon reappointment by the appointing party. The chairman of the board was the legal representative of the joint venture enterprise. After the Joint Venture Contract was signed, Bao Yangbo served as the chairman of Taihua Company. On October 22 of the same year, the State Administration for Industry and Commerce of the People's Republic of China issued the enterprise legal person business license to Taihua Company.

Some time after Taihua Company was established, Materials Company transferred its 10% share in Taihua Company to Shangqiao Company. On March 30, 1994, Bao Yangbo and Wu Shenggang (a Taiwanese) signed a "Share Transfer Agreement", whereby Bao Yangbo transferred his 50% share in Taihua Company to Wu Shenggang, and Wu Shenggang authorized Bao Yangbo with full power to handle all matters of Taihua Company on his behalf. On April 1, 1994, the board of directors of Taihua Company decided that Wu Shenggang would serve as the chairman. On June 14 of the same year, Taihua Company reported to the Chongqing Municipal Administration for Industry and Commerce (hereinafter referred to as the Municipal Administration for Industry and Commerce) to change the chairman and legal representative to Wu Shenggang. On July 23, 1996, Bao Yangbo, as the fully authorized agent of Wu Shenggang, signed a share transfer contract with Chongqing Chenguang Industrial Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Chenguang Industrial), agreeing that Wu Shenggang would transfer his 50% share in Taihua Company to Chenguang Industrial for a price of RMB 13.1 million. Chenguang Industrial paid RMB 8 million and RMB 4.1 million to Bao Yangbo on July 24 and August 1 of the same year, respectively. On July 24 of the same year, Shangqiao Company also signed a "Share Transfer Contract" with Chenguang Industrial, transferring its 50% share in Taihua Company to Chenguang Industrial.

On July 24, 1996, Bao Yangbo, as the fully authorized agent of Wu Shenggang, together with Shangqiao Company, delivered the entire existing commercial podium building of the Fuhao Commercial Plaza developed by Taihua Company to Chenguang Industrial in its current condition, along with the seal of Taihua Company. Subsequently, Chenguang Industrial changed its name to Chenguang Group in December 1996, renamed the Fuhao Commercial Plaza as Chenguang Building, and then began investing in it, adding facilities, equipment, decoration, and finishing. On December 2, 1998, Chenguang Group applied for and obtained the certificate of title to the building in the name of Taihua Company. The certificate indicated that the building usage was non-residential commercial premises, with a gross floor area of 15,654.74 square meters. After Chenguang Industrial acquired Taihua Company, it did not change the legal representative of Taihua Company.

In 1997, Wu Shenggang filed a lawsuit with the Chongqing First Intermediate People's Court (hereinafter referred to as the First Intermediate Court) on the grounds that the original Chenguang Industrial (now Chenguang Group) had not paid the balance of the share transfer price of RMB 1 million, requesting a judgment that the share transfer was invalid and that Wu Shenggang should return to Taihua Company to continue serving as the chairman. On May 14, 1999, the First Intermediate Court rendered a civil judgment (1997) Yu Yi Zhong Jing Chu Zi No. 1055, holding that Wu Shenggang was not the legal owner of the 50% share in Taihua Company, did not have the subject-matter qualification to transfer shares to Chenguang Industrial (now Chenguang Group), and had not fulfilled the required formal legal acts for the share transfer to take effect under the law. Therefore, the share transfer between the parties was invalid, and the primary responsibility for the invalidity of the transfer was borne by Wu Shenggang. The court then ruled that the share transfer contract signed between Wu Shenggang and Chenguang Industrial (now Chenguang Group) was invalid and rejected Wu Shenggang's other claims.

At the end of 1999, Bao Yangbo, in accordance with the arbitration clause in the Joint Venture Contract, applied for arbitration with the Shenzhen Sub-Commission of the China International Economic and Trade Arbitration Commission. On April 25, 2001, the commission issued an award (2001) Shen Guo Zhong Jie Zi No. 31, ruling that the share transfers between Materials Company and Shangqiao Company, and between Shangqiao Company and Chenguang Industrial (now Chenguang Group), were invalid; ordering Chenguang Group to immediately withdraw from Taihua Company and return the management and operation rights of Taihua Company; and stipulating that the chairman of Taihua Company should be appointed by Bao Yangbo in accordance with the Joint Venture Contract. Because Chenguang Group did not comply with this arbitration award, on May 22, 2001, Bao Yangbo applied to the First Intermediate Court for compulsory enforcement. On June 4 of the same year, Chenguang Group applied to the First Intermediate Court for a refusal to enforce the arbitration award. After review, the court issued a civil ruling (2001) Yu Yi Zhong Min Ta Zhi Zi No. 247-1, ruling that items 2, 3, 5, and 7 of Award (2001) Shen Guo Zhong Jie Zi No. 31 of the Shenzhen Sub-Commission of the China International Economic and Trade Arbitration Commission would not be enforced.

On July 19, 2001, Chenguang Group filed a lawsuit with the First Intermediate Court against Wu Shenggang as the defendant, requesting a judgment that Wu Shenggang return the already received share transfer price of RMB 12.1 million and compensate for the loss of use of the funds. On September 10, 2002, the First Intermediate Court rendered a civil judgment (2001) Yu Yi Zhong Min Chu Zi No. 437, supporting the claims of Chenguang Group. This judgment has now become effective, but it cannot be enforced because Wu Shenggang is a Taiwanese national.

In 2001, Chenguang Group filed a lawsuit with the First Intermediate Court against Shangqiao Company, requesting a judgment that Shangqiao Company return the share transfer price of RMB 17 million. After winning the case, Chenguang Group applied to the First Intermediate Court for enforcement. Because Shangqiao Company had no other executable property, the parties, under the auspices of the First Intermediate Court, voluntarily reached a settlement agreement, whereby Shangqiao Company used its 50% share in Taihua Company to offset the share transfer price. Shangqiao Company also issued a written authorization to Chenguang Group to exercise its rights in the shareholders' meeting and board of directors of Taihua Company and to participate in the decision-making of Taihua Company as a full-representative shareholder.

In July 2001, Chenguang Group filed a lawsuit with the First Intermediate Court against Taihua Company, requesting a judgment that Taihua Company return invested funds of RMB 31,720,045.53. On September 10 of the same year, the First Intermediate Court, by way of default judgment, rendered a civil judgment (2001) Yu Yi Zhong Min Chu Zi No. 353, ordering Taihua Company to return the invested funds of RMB 31,720,045.53. On September 10, 2001, Chenguang Group filed another lawsuit with the First Intermediate Court against Taihua Company, requesting a judgment that Taihua Company pay interest on the invested funds of RMB 13,993,887.40. On December 7 of the same year, the First Intermediate Court, also by way of default judgment, rendered a civil judgment (2001) Yu Yi Zhong Min Chu Zi No. 550, ordering Taihua Company to pay Chenguang Group interest on the invested funds of RMB 13,993,887.40. When enforcement proceedings commenced on the above two judgments, Bao Yangbo became aware of these two lawsuits and filed complaints with the First Intermediate Court and the Chongqing Municipal People's Procuratorate (hereinafter referred to as the Municipal Procuratorate). After accepting the cases, the Municipal Procuratorate filed civil protests (2002) Yu Jian Min Kang Zi No. 11 and No. 12. Upon instruction from the Chongqing High People's Court, the First Intermediate Court retried the cases. During the retrial, the First Intermediate Court commissioned an audit department to audit the funds (including debt repayments) invested by Chenguang Group in Taihua Company after Chenguang Group took over Taihua Company on July 24, 1996, and commissioned Chongqing Huitong Asset Appraisal Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Huitong Appraisal Company) to appraise the assets invested by Chenguang Group in Taihua Company after the takeover on July 24, 1996. The accounting books and other appraisal materials provided by Chenguang Group to Huitong Appraisal Company included materials related to the Trustee Center, Chenguang Group, Chenguang Department Store, and Chenguang Hotel. After appraisal, the conclusion was that the appraisal value of equipment and facilities invested by Chenguang Company in the Chenguang Building from July 24, 1996, to April 3, 2003, was RMB 7,044,128.56, the appraisal value of decoration and finishing was RMB 2,417,166.06, and the total appraisal value was RMB 9,461,294.62.

On December 18, 2003, the First Intermediate Court rendered a civil judgment (2002) Yu Yi Zhong Min Zai Chu Zi No. 385, ordering Taihua Company to return to Chenguang Group the fruits of the investment funds of RMB 12,750,782 and the fruits of the debts repaid by Chenguang Group on behalf of Taihua Company of RMB 650,000 (calculated from September 10, 1998, until payment is made, at the benchmark loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the corresponding period). On the same day, the First Intermediate Court rendered a civil judgment (2002) Yu Yi Zhong Min Zai Chu Zi No. 386, ordering Taihua Company to return to Chenguang Group the investment funds of RMB 10,210,864.39 and to compensate Chenguang Group for the loss of improvements to the Chenguang Building of RMB 8,515,165.10. In both cases, Wu Shenggang, in his capacity as the legal representative of Taihua Company, authorized agent Dong Jiawei to participate in the proceedings in the name of Taihua Company. After the two judgments were rendered, Taihua Company, dissatisfied, appealed to the Chongqing High People's Court, and the cases are currently under trial at the second instance.

The court of first instance also found: On February 5, 2001, the Chongqing Municipal Joint Annual Inspection Office for Foreign-Invested Enterprises published the "Announcement on the Joint Annual Inspection of Foreign-Invested Enterprises for 2000 and the Replacement of Business Licenses and Registration Certificates" in the Chongqing Evening News, requiring "three types of enterprises" (Sino-foreign joint ventures, cooperative enterprises, and wholly foreign-owned enterprises) in Chongqing to undergo annual inspection before April 30 of the same year, failing which they would be dealt with according to law. On May 15 of the same year, Bao Yangbo submitted an application to the Municipal Administration for Industry and Commerce to change the registration of the chairman. The Municipal Administration for Industry and Commerce considered that Bao Yangbo was not a qualified applicant and did not process it. On June 8 of the same year, the Municipal Administration for Industry and Commerce published the "Announcement on Supplementary Annual Inspection for Foreign-Invested Enterprises for 2000" in the Chongqing Commercial Newspaper. Taihua Company still did not apply for annual inspection. On August 30 of the same year, the Municipal Administration for Industry and Commerce published the "Hearing Announcement on the Revocation of Business Licenses of Foreign-Invested Enterprises That Did Not Undergo Annual Inspection for 2000" in the Chongqing Commercial Newspaper. Taihua Company did not participate in the hearing. On December 18 of the same year, the Municipal Administration for Industry and Commerce issued an Administrative Penalty Decision (Zhong Gong Shang Wai Chu Zi (2001) No. 313), deciding to revoke the legal person business license of Taihua Company on the grounds that it had not undergone annual inspection according to law. Wu Shenggang, through his agent Dong Jiawei, in the name of Taihua Company, challenged this decision and applied to the Chongqing Municipal People's Government for administrative reconsideration. After review, the Chongqing Municipal People's Government found that: The legal representative of Taihua Company was Wu Shenggang. Although the dispute between the original investor Bao Yangbo of Taihua Company and Chenguang Group had been settled by arbitration, and the dispute between Wu Shenggang and Chenguang Group had also been resolved by court judgment, the industrial and commercial registration still showed Wu Shenggang as the legal representative, and Wu Shenggang remained the current lawful legal representative. After the Municipal Administration for Industry and Commerce published its announcements, neither Wu Shenggang nor Taihua Company submitted an application for annual inspection or any comments. Only Bao Yangbo submitted an application for a change of registration of the chairman, but Bao Yangbo was not a qualified applicant. In the absence of any opinion from the board of directors or the legal representative, the Municipal Administration for Industry and Commerce was unable to make a decision to change the registration of the chairman. Taihua Company could not refuse the annual inspection on the grounds of internal economic disputes. The government then issued an Administrative Reconsideration Decision (Yu Fu Fu (2002) No. 99), deciding to uphold the penalty decision Zhong Gong Shang Wai Chu Zi (2001) No. 313. Taihua Company did not file a lawsuit with the court within the statutory period after receiving the decision, and the decision became effective.

Further found: Chenguang Industrial was established in October 1995 with a capital contribution of RMB 8 million from Chongqing Shapingba District Investment Company and RMB 4 million from Chongqing Shapingba District Real Estate Development General Company. In October 1996, Chenguang Industrial contributed RMB 3 million and Chongqing Shapingba Investment Company contributed RMB 2 million to establish Chongqing Chenguang Department Store Co., Ltd. On November 25, 1996, Chenguang Industrial contributed RMB 2 million (fixed assets) and Chenguang Department Store contributed RMB 1 million to establish Chongqing Chenguang Hotel Co., Ltd. In December 1996, Chongqing Shapingba District Investment Company contributed RMB 8 million, Taihua Company contributed RMB 4.5 million, Chongqing Huaye Plastic Products Co., Ltd. contributed RMB 3 million, Chenguang Department Store contributed RMB 3 million, and Nanchong Jincheng Co., Ltd. contributed RMB 1.5 million to establish Chenguang Group, with a registered capital of RMB 20 million. On January 3, 1997, Taihua Company and Chenguang Hotel signed a "House Lease Contract", agreeing to lease operating premises with a total floor area of 11,000 square meters in the Chenguang Building to Chenguang Hotel for free for a period of 20 years, i.e., from January 1997 to January 2017. Because Chongqing Shapingba District Investment Company was a "three-disorder" financial institution, from April 1999 to the present, the Trustee Center of Chongqing Shapingba District People's Government District Investment Company (hereinafter referred to as the Trustee Center) has been entrusted with the assets of all enterprises established by Chongqing Shapingba District Investment Company, including Chenguang Group, Chenguang Department Store, Taihua Company, and Chongqing Yudong Plastics Factory.

The initiation of this lawsuit was conducted by Wu Shenggang, in his capacity as the legal representative of Taihua Company, authorizing agent Dong Jiawei to proceed. The complaint in this case does not bear the seal of Taihua Company, and the signature of the legal representative was signed by Dong Jiawei on his behalf.

Taihua Company filed a lawsuit with the court of first instance, requesting a judgment ordering: Chenguang Group, Chenguang Department Store, and Chenguang Hotel to immediately vacate and return to Taihua Company the Chenguang Building located at No. 1 Yuzhou Road, Gaoxin District, Chongqing, which is owned by Taihua Company; and that all litigation costs in this case be borne by Chenguang Group, Chenguang Department Store, and Chenguang Hotel.

Chenguang Group argued in defense that Taihua Company's lawsuit had neither factual basis nor legal basis, and that the plaintiff's qualification was improper, requesting that the lawsuit be dismissed according to law.

Chenguang Department Store and Chenguang Hotel argued in defense that there was no fact of them occupying the premises of Taihua Company, and that they had no fault in the entire matter and should not bear any alleged joint and several liability. They requested that Taihua Company's claims be dismissed according to law.

After trial, the court of first instance held that the main issues in dispute between the parties were: 1. Whether Wu Shenggang could exercise the right of action on behalf of Taihua Company; 2. Whether Taihua Company was a proper plaintiff in this case.

1. Wu Shenggang could not exercise the right of action on behalf of Taihua Company. The reasons are as follows: The civil judgment (1997) Yu Yi Zhong Jing Chu Zi No. 1055 determined that Wu Shenggang was not a shareholder of Taihua Company and rejected Wu Shenggang's request to return to Taihua Company to serve as chairman. At the end of 1999, Bao Yangbo, on the grounds that Wu Shenggang had been confirmed by the effective judgment No. 1055 as not being a lawful shareholder of Taihua Company, applied for arbitration and requested a confirmation that he (Bao Yangbo) should be the chairman of Taihua Company. The arbitration award stipulated that the chairman of Taihua Company should be appointed by Bao Yangbo in accordance with the Joint Venture Contract. Bao Yangbo did not perform the duty of appointment after receiving the award. According to the Joint Venture Contract signed on September 20, 1992, by Shangqiao Company, Materials Company, and Bao Yangbo, the board of directors of the joint venture enterprise consisted of three members, each appointed by the three shareholders (Shangqiao Company, Materials Company, and Bao Yangbo). The chairman was appointed by Bao Yangbo. The term of office for directors and the chairman was three years, renewable upon reappointment by the appointing party. The chairman was the legal representative of the joint venture enterprise. That is to say, Wu Shenggang had served as the chairman of Taihua Company from April 1, 1994, and his term expired on April 2, 1997. Therefore, the position of chairman of Taihua Company had been vacant since April 2, 1997. Wu Shenggang was neither a shareholder of Taihua Company nor a member of the board of directors of the joint venture enterprise. His term as chairman of Taihua Company had expired. According to the provisions of the Joint Venture Contract and the Implementing Regulations of the Law of the People's Republic of China on Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Ventures, a person who is not the chairman of the board is not the legal representative of the joint venture enterprise. Although the current industrial and commercial registration shows Wu Shenggang as the legal representative of Taihua Company, in substance, Wu Shenggang was no longer the legal representative of Taihua Company. Therefore, Wu Shenggang could not exercise the right of action on behalf of Taihua Company.

2. Taihua Company is not a proper plaintiff in this case. The reasons are as follows: In October 1995, Chenguang Industry was established with capital contributed by Chongqing Shapingba District Investment Company. In July 1996, Chenguang Industry acquired 100% of the equity interest in Taihua Company through assignment. Chongqing Shapingba District Investment Company was a financial institution involved in illegal fund-raising, financial disorder, and illegal financial operations ("three disorder" institutions). In April 1999, both Chenguang Industry and Taihua Company were included in the scope of clean-up and rectification. Taihua Company was unable to continue its operations, and when Wu Shenggang, in the capacity of Taihua Company's legal representative, entrusted agent Dong Jiawei to initiate this lawsuit in the name of Taihua Company, the term of the joint venture of Taihua Company had already expired. For Taihua Company, both statutory and agreed causes for dissolution had arisen. It should have established a liquidation committee and settled its claims and debts in accordance with Articles 91 and 93 of the Implementing Regulations for the Law of the People's Republic of China on Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Ventures and the provisions of the Joint Venture Contract.

In summary, pursuant to Article 140, paragraph 1, item (3) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the ruling is as follows: The lawsuit of Taihua Company is dismissed. The case acceptance fee of RMB 50 shall be borne by Taihua Company.

Taihua Company, dissatisfied with the first-instance ruling, appealed to this Court, requesting that the first-instance ruling be reversed, that its claims at first instance be sustained by judgment, or that the case be transferred to a court in a different locality for trial. Its main reasons were: After Taihua Company's business license was revoked, because the company had no external debts, the company's shareholders did not and for the time being were unwilling to organize a liquidation group for the company's liquidation, and all of them had explicitly or implicitly recognized the relevant litigation actions. Taihua Company had the capacity to be a plaintiff in the lawsuit. Wu Shenggang could represent or entrust an agent to represent Taihua Company in the litigation. According to the legislative intent of the relevant laws, revocation is one of the causes for cancellation, but it does not equal cancellation. Taihua Company's legal personality had not been extinguished. An enterprise whose business license has been revoked may still, in its own name, settle its claims and debts through litigation. According to the industrial and commercial registration, the legal representative of Taihua Company was Wu Shenggang, and Wu Shenggang could still perform the duties of the legal representative of Taihua Company. Wu Shenggang's representation of Taihua Company in the litigation did not and would not infringe upon the rights and interests of Taihua Company or its shareholders. Furthermore, under the provisions of the current Company Law, the dissolution of a company does not include the situation where the company's business license is revoked. Wu Shenggang's special entrustment of an agent to represent Taihua Company in the litigation was genuine and lawful. In the absence of a company seal, Wu Shenggang could only entrust an agent for litigation by signature. The relevant entrustment formalities had already been "notarized" and "authenticated." Therefore, Taihua Company's claims had factual and legal basis, and the first-instance court should have rendered a judgment on the merits.

Chenguang Group, Chenguang Department Store, and Chenguang Hotel responded in defense, arguing that the first-instance ruling had clear findings of fact and correct application of law, and requested that the appeal be dismissed and the original ruling be affirmed.

This Court found upon further investigation in the second instance: The power of attorney for Dong Jiawei to participate in the proceedings was personally signed and acknowledged by Wu Shenggang himself, and the authorization for litigation was special authorization. The complaint at first instance and the appeal petition in this second instance were written by Dong Jiawei, in which Wu Shenggang's signature was affixed by Dong Jiawei on his behalf. During the trial in the second instance, this Court sought the opinions of both parties on how to address this issue. Chenguang Group, Chenguang Department Store, and Chenguang Hotel stated that they no longer had any objection to the authenticity of the entrustment and authorization of Taihua Company's agent ad litem. Separately, both parties acknowledged in court during the second instance the fact that Taihua Company's official seal was currently held by Chenguang Group.

Other facts found by this Court in the second instance are substantially the same as those found by the court of first instance.

Opinion of the Court: The disputes in this case mainly involve two issues: (1) whether Taihua Company has the capacity to be the plaintiff in this case; and (2) whether Wu Shenggang has the authority to exercise litigation rights on behalf of Taihua Company.

(1) Whether Taihua Company has the capacity to be the plaintiff in this case. Taihua Company was an enterprise legal person lawfully registered and established on October 22, 1992. At that time, the chairman of the board of directors, i.e., the legal representative of Taihua Company, was Bao Yangbo. Subsequently, on June 14, 1994, the chairman of the board of directors of Taihua Company was changed to Wu Shenggang, which remains the case to date. On December 18, 2001, the Municipal Administration for Industry and Commerce revoked Taihua Company's business license of an enterprise legal person because Taihua Company had failed to undergo annual inspection according to law, but did not cancel the registration of Taihua Company. As an independent enterprise legal person, whether Taihua Company's legal personality continues to exist should be determined by whether the administrative authority for industry and commerce has already cancelled its registration. Even though the term of the joint venture of Taihua Company had expired as stipulated in the Joint Venture Contract, as long as its registration has not been cancelled, its legal personality cannot be denied. Revocation of the business license of an enterprise legal person is an administrative penalty imposed by the administrative authority for industry and commerce on a non-compliant enterprise legal person in accordance with national administrative regulations on industry and commerce. After an enterprise legal person's business license is revoked, it shall proceed with liquidation according to law. Only after the liquidation procedure is completed and the industrial and commercial cancellation registration is processed does the enterprise legal person cease to exist. During the period from the revocation of the business license of an enterprise legal person to the cancellation of its registration, the enterprise legal person should still be regarded as existing and may engage in litigation activities in its own name. Therefore, Taihua Company, even after its business license was revoked, still has the capacity for litigation rights and capacity for litigation conduct, and has the right to initiate civil litigation in its own name. The fact that Taihua Company has not established a liquidation organization should not be a reason to restrict its participation in civil litigation. The first-instance ruling, which held that Taihua Company did not have the capacity to be a plaintiff, incorrectly applied the law.

(2) Whether Wu Shenggang has the authority to exercise litigation rights on behalf of Taihua Company. According to Taihua Company's registration with the administrative authority for industry and commerce, Wu Shenggang remains the legal representative of Taihua Company to date. In the absence of a liquidation organization established by Taihua Company, Wu Shenggang may exercise the powers of the legal representative of Taihua Company. Even in light of the content of the arbitration award, Bao Yangbo did not appoint another legal representative in accordance with the Joint Venture Contract. Under the circumstance where both parties acknowledge that Taihua Company's official seal is held by Chenguang Group, as long as Wu Shenggang, as the legal representative, has a genuine intention to exercise the right of action in the name of Taihua Company and complies with legal provisions, Wu Shenggang may exercise the right of action in the name of Taihua Company. Therefore, the first-instance ruling's reasoning that Wu Shenggang could not represent Taihua Company in initiating the lawsuit is erroneous. Furthermore, although Wu Shenggang did not directly participate in the litigation, he has entrusted a litigation agent to exercise his litigation rights, and the authenticity of the entrustment formalities has been acknowledged by the opposing party. Therefore, there is no obstacle to Taihua Company's initiation of this lawsuit.

In summary, the first-instance ruling dismissing Taihua Company's lawsuit applied the law incorrectly and should be corrected. Pursuant to Articles 108 and 154 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 187 of the Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the ruling is as follows:

1. The civil ruling (2003) Yu Gao Fa Min Chu Zi No. 12 of the Chongqing High People's Court is reversed;

2. The case shall be tried by the Chongqing High People's Court.

Presiding Judge: Han Mei
Acting Judge: Jia Jinsong
Acting Judge: Xin Zhengyu

September 20, 2005

Clerk: Wang Dongying

[Profile of the Presiding Judge]

Han Mei, Senior Judge: Born in 1962, Master of Laws. Appointed as Judge of the Supreme People's Court in 2000.
